title_en: Daqing Kaiming Wind Power Tower Manufacturing Co., Ltd. v. Sinovel Wind Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over sales contract
ruling_gist_en: Contracts must be strictly observed. If the order of performance of contractual obligations is sequential, and the party obliged to perform first fails to perform, thereby making it difficult for the other party to perform its obligations, the latter party acquires the right to defense of prior performance and is entitled to demand full performance of the contract from the former party.

full_text_en:
Daqing Kaiming Wind Power Tower Manufacturing Co., Ltd. v. Huarui Wind Power Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. — dispute over a general sales contract

Ruling Summary

A contract must be strictly observed. Where a contract provides for a sequential order of performance, and the party obliged to perform first fails to perform, thereby creating difficulties for the other party to perform its obligations, the latter party thereby acquires the right to plead the prior performance defense and is entitled to require the former party to perform all its obligations under the contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2013) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 181

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff): Huarui Wind Power Technology (Group) Co., Ltd., domiciled at 19/F, Wenhua Building, No. 59 Zhongguancun Street, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal representative: Wang Yuan, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Kou Liyun, lawyer with Beijing Global Law Office.

Agent ad litem: Wen Gaolian, lawyer with Beijing Tongshuo Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant): Daqing Kaiming Wind Power Tower Manufacturing Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 28 Xinfa Street, High-tech Zone (Development Zone), Daqing City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal representative: Zhang Qingsheng, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Yalan, lawyer with Heilongjiang Longdian Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Guoxin, lawyer with Heilongjiang Chaoyue Law Firm.

The appellant, Huarui Wind Power Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huarui Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2012) Hei Gao Shang Chu Zi No. 9 rendered by the High People's Court of Heilongjiang Province (hereinafter referred to as Heilongjiang High Court) in a dispute over a general sales contract with the appellee, Daqing Kaiming Wind Power Tower Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kaiming Company). After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing on November 29, 2013. The agents ad litem of Huarui Company, Kou Liyun and Wen Gaolian, and the agents ad litem of Kaiming Company, Li Yalan and Zhao Guoxin, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

The following facts were ascertained in the first instance trial by the Heilongjiang High Court:

On September 5, 2010, Kaiming Company and Huarui Company entered into the "Huarui Wind Power SL3000/HH90 Onshore Low-Temperature Tower Sales Contract" (WX3MW10009) (hereinafter referred to as the Tower Sales Contract), stipulating that Kaiming Company would sell to Huarui Company 64 sets of 3MW onshore low-temperature towers (including towers, foundation rings, and steel structures inside the towers). The contract was to be performed in two phases: 32 sets were to be delivered before March 1, 2011. The contract price was RMB 12,140 per ton, with each tower tentatively set at 305.75 tons, for a total price of RMB 3,711,805 per tower, and a total contract price of RMB 237,555,520. The final total price was to be based on the tonnage verified by both parties in accordance with the buyer's drawings. The contract price included costs for equipment, technical materials, technical services, taxes, freight, insurance, and other expenses related to the contract. Delivery was to be ex-works at the Daqing Heping Ranch vehicle deck. It was also agreed that "when the market prices of steel plates and flanges fluctuate by more than or equal to 5% from the prices of steel plates and flanges specified in Appendix 1, the supply price shall be adjusted accordingly." Appendix 1 stated that the weight of the tower steel plates was 261 tons, and according to the drawings, the average price per ton of tower steel plates was RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% wastage). Payment was to be made by bank wire transfer or acceptance draft. Huarui Company would pay a 10% advance payment of the total price for Phase I, i.e., RMB 11,877,776, within 15 days after receiving the financial receipt for 10% of the total Phase I price submitted by Kaiming Company. Thirty days before the delivery of Phase I contracted equipment, Kaiming Company would submit to Huarui Company financial instruments for 20% of the total Phase I price; within 30 days after Huarui Company verified them as correct, Huarui Company would pay 20% of the total Phase I price, i.e., RMB 23,755,552. After all foundation rings for Phase I had arrived at the site and passed inspection, and within 15 days after Huarui Company received the 30% receipt and the equipment arrival acceptance certificate signed by both parties, Huarui Company would pay 30% of the total Phase I price, i.e., RMB 35,633,328. After 16 sets of tower units had arrived at the site and passed inspection, and within 15 days after Huarui Company received the 15% receipt and the equipment arrival acceptance certificate signed by both parties, Huarui Company would pay 15% of the total Phase I price, i.e., RMB 17,816,664. After the other 16 sets had arrived and passed inspection, and within 15 days after Huarui Company received the 15% receipt, the full 100% invoice for the Phase I total price, and the equipment arrival acceptance certificate signed by both parties, Huarui Company would pay 15% of the total Phase I price, i.e., RMB 17,816,664. Within 30 days after the one-year warranty period following tower installation expired, Huarui Company would pay the 10% balance, i.e., RMB 11,877,776. The price and payment terms for Phase II were the same as for Phase I. Kaiming Company was required to deliver the goods and provide services in accordance with the time stipulated in the contract. If Kaiming Company delayed delivery without justifiable cause, a penalty for delay and/or contract termination for breach would be imposed. If Kaiming Company encountered circumstances that might prevent timely delivery and provision of services, it was to promptly notify Huarui Company in writing of the facts of the delay, the probable duration of the delay, and the reasons therefor. Huarui Company was to evaluate the situation promptly and determine whether to agree to extend the delivery time and whether to impose a delay penalty. The extension was to be mutually agreed upon by the parties through a contract amendment. The penalty was to be calculated at 0.5% of the value of the delayed goods for the first week, and 1% for the second week, with a maximum penalty not exceeding 5% of the contract price for the goods. Unless agreed to by Huarui Company, Kaiming Company was not to subcontract all or part of the equipment under the contract to a third party; if it did so in breach of contract, Huarui Company had the right to make a claim under Article 14 of the contract. The contract was to become effective upon signature by the legal representatives or authorized agents of both parties and affixing of the contract seals, and would take immediate effect from the date the approval document for the wind farm project was issued. On December 6, 2010, the Heilongjiang Provincial Development and Reform Commission approved the Daqing Heping Ranch wind farm project.

On November 2, 2010, Huarui Company notified Kaiming Company by fax that, due to the accelerated construction progress of the Daqing Heping Ranch project, the delivery date for foundation rings as stipulated in the contract was changed from March 1, 2011, to January 15 to March 15, 2011; the delivery date for tower bodies and accessories was changed from March 1, 2011, to March 15 to June 15, 2011; and the quantity to be delivered was changed from 32 sets to 64 sets. On November 3, 2011, Kaiming Company replied to Huarui Company, stating that it had received the notice regarding the change in delivery deadline and quantity, that it had already signed procurement contracts with flange and steel plate suppliers but needed to pay a down payment, and that if Huarui Company could not pay the first advance payment for the 64 sets within 5 days, the supply period for flanges and steel plates would be delayed by one month, and consequently the supply period for foundation rings and towers would also be delayed by one month. Both parties jointly confirmed that after the delivery period was advanced, the advance payment and progress payments would still be made according to the conditions and ratios stipulated in the contract, but the calculation of supply quantity and payment amount should be based on the standard of 64 sets of towers. During actual performance, the condition for Kaiming Company to issue receipts was changed to: before Huarui Company made payment, Kaiming Company would issue a receipt for the amount actually payable by Huarui Company. Kaiming Company issued the corresponding receipts as agreed.

On January 26, 2011, Kaiming Company sent to Huarui Company a "Letter Regarding the Release of the Contract Advance Payment for the Daqing Heping Ranch 3.0 MW Wind Turbine Tower Project and Confirmation of Tower Price Adjustment," stating: "In accordance with the contract, your company should pay our company a 10% advance payment of the total contract price after the contract takes effect, totaling RMB 23.75 million. However, your company only paid RMB 14 million on December 23, 2010. Despite the fact that your company has not yet paid the remaining RMB 9.75 million advance payment, our company actively ordered raw materials and has now ordered all flanges for the 64 sets of towers, paying RMB 14 million in advance payments. We have also ordered about 1,040 tons of steel plates for the foundation rings of the 64 sets and test plates, paying RMB 7 million for the goods. During this period, our company has repeatedly negotiated with suppliers regarding the ordering of the remaining steel plates. The lowest average price for ordering steel plates obtained so far (including freight and tax) is RMB 6,197 per ton. According to the contract, when the market price of steel plates fluctuates by more than the agreed 5%, the supply price of finished tower products shall be adjusted accordingly. The average price of steel plates in the tower price composition is RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% wastage); after excluding wastage, the average procurement price of steel plates (including freight and tax) is RMB 5,700.57 per ton (RMB 6,042.6 ÷ 1.06 = RMB 5,700.57). The current market price has risen by 8.71% compared to the steel plate price agreed upon at the time of signing the contract. In view of the above, please expedite the payment of the remaining advanced payment of RMB 9.75 million for the project. At the same time, please confirm the adjustment to the unit price of finished towers due to the rise in steel plate prices. The price adjustment may also be calculated based on our company's final actual purchase price. If your company fails to give a written reply before January 26, 2011, our company will consider that your company has confirmed and agreed to the above matters, and our company will sign a steel plate procurement contract with the supplier to ensure timely supply." Huarui Company replied on the same day: "Please immediately order the remaining steel plates to avoid delaying the delivery date. Our company will contact the project owner as soon as possible regarding the remaining advance payment and pay your company as early as possible. We sincerely apologize for this. The matter of contract price adjustment will be discussed later." On February 15, 2011, Kaiming Company again wrote to Huarui Company regarding the advance payment and tower price adjustment, stating: "On January 26, 2011, our company sent a letter and obtained your company's consent. We then advanced another RMB 13.47 million to order 64 sets of tower plates of 54mm specification. To date, the total advanced funds for the procurement of steel plates for this project amount to RMB 20.775 million. Recently, our company has repeatedly negotiated with suppliers regarding the ordering of all remaining steel plates. The current average price for ordering all remaining steel plates (including freight and tax) has reached RMB 6,196 per ton; for door frames, it has reached RMB 19,860.35 per ton, and there is still a strong upward trend. If calculated at this price, the cost of the procurement to be made this time will reach RMB 91.29 million. According to the contract between the parties, when the market price of steel plates fluctuates by more than the agreed 5%, the supply price of finished towers shall be adjusted accordingly. The average price of steel plates in the tower price composition is RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% wastage); after excluding wastage, the average procurement price of steel plates (including freight and tax) is RMB 5,700.57 per ton (steel plate price = RMB 6,042.6 / 1.06 = RMB 5,700.57). If this procurement plan is implemented, the average price per ton of all steel plates used in the entire project will reach RMB 6,640, a price increase of 13%. At present, for this project, our company has already advanced RMB 20.775 million for steel plates alone. Given the actual situation of our company, we are unable to proceed with this steel plate procurement (RMB 91.29 million). In view of the above, please expedite payment of the remaining advance payment of RMB 9.75 million and the material preparation payment of RMB 47.52 million. At the same time, please confirm the adjustment to the unit price of finished towers due to the rise in steel plate prices. The price adjustment may also be calculated based on our company's final actual purchase price. If your company fails to give a written reply before February 17, 2011, our company will consider that your company has confirmed and agreed to the above matters, and our company will wait for your company to pay the corresponding amounts before signing a steel plate procurement contract with the supplier to ensure timely delivery." Kaiming Company also sent letters to Huarui Company on March 15, September 28, November 3, November 11, December 1, and December 5, 2011, and on March 28, 2012, requesting Huarui Company to pay the outstanding amounts, failing which it would stop supply. In reply to the letter of December 5, 2011, Huarui Company stated that its payable amount was RMB 71,266,656, it had paid RMB 61,555,552, and the remaining RMB 9,711,104 would be paid that week. Because Kaiming Company had not issued valid quality certification documents for the foundation rings, and Kaiming Company was unable to provide a third-party inspection report for the 32 sets of foundation rings with quality issues, nor had it issued a quality undertaking letter, the RMB 71,266,656 for foundation ring delivery and RMB 17,816,664 for tower delivery claimed by Kaiming Company were temporarily not due. On December 21, 2011, Huarui Company notified Kaiming Company that the supply of the subsequent 32 sets of towers should refer to the equipment hoisting progress schedule of Daqing Lvyuan Wind Power Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lvyuan Company) project. Kaiming Company was to prepare a production plan before December 22, 2011, and notify Huarui Company. On February 21, 2012, Huarui Company notified Kaiming Company to supply towers at a rate of one set every two days from that date. On March 19, 2012, Huarui Company notified Kaiming Company to deliver the 48th to 64th sets of towers to the site in installments from March 19 to April 22, 2012, according to the hoisting site progress requirements. On April 20, 2012, Huarui Company notified Kaiming Company to adjust the unit price of towers from RMB 12,104 per ton to RMB 9,950 per ton. On July 20 and August 8, 2012, Huarui Company twice notified Kaiming Company to come to its office to negotiate the hoisting downtime compensation, handle the procedures for changing the contract price, and supply the remaining 9 tower bodies. On August 16, 2012, Kaiming Company sent to Huarui Company a "Reply Letter Regarding Performance Issues under the Tower Sales Contract," requesting Huarui Company to continue performing the contract, accept the remaining 9 tower bodies, pay the outstanding amounts, and confirm the adjustment to the tower price. On September 3, 2012, Huarui Company replied to Kaiming Company, stating that the Tower Sales Contract was signed on the basis of the "49.5MW Wind Power Project Wind Turbine Generator Set Sales Contract" (Zhaoyuan Xinlong Shunde) and the "Wind Turbine Generator Set Sales Agreement" signed between Kaiming New Energy Company and Huarui Company. Since Kaiming Company unilaterally revoked these two contracts, the tower procurement price and related terms agreed upon by the parties could not be established. On October 25, 2012, Huarui Company again wrote to Kaiming Company, requesting Kaiming Company to come to Beijing to negotiate the delay penalty, the change of the contract price, and the supply of the remaining towers.

It was further ascertained that on October 30, 2010, Kaiming Company entered into a sales contract with Qinhuangdao Aotong Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aotong Company); on January 30, 2011, with Qinhuangdao Zhaojia Yu Industry and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhaojia Yu Company); and on February 23, 2011, with Daqing High-tech Zone Huahong Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huahong Company). Through these contracts, Kaiming Company purchased a total of 17,350 tons of steel plates of models including Q345E, paying a total of RMB 109,304,462.58. The average price per ton of the plates purchased was RMB 6,300.

Huarui Company made payments as follows: RMB 10 million on November 29, 2010; RMB 4 million on December 13, 2010; RMB 9,755,552 on March 2, 2011; RMB 20 million on April 26, 2011; RMB 17.8 million on November 28, 2011; RMB 37,833,328 on December 16, 2011; RMB 20 million on December 31, 2011; and RMB 5 million on April 6, 2012. The total payments amounted to RMB 124,388,880.

Kaiming Company began delivering foundation rings on April 22, 2011. In April, it delivered 4 sets; in June, 11 sets; in July, 10 sets; in August, 7 sets; in September, 26 sets; and in October, 6 sets, totaling 64 sets. Kaiming Company delivered tower bodies as follows: 2 sets in August 2011; 2 sets in September; 6 sets in October; 9 sets in November; 12 sets in December; 4 sets in January 2012; 8 sets in February; 9 sets in March; and 3 sets in April, totaling 55 sets.

On January 31, 2012, Huarui Company entered into a contract with Harbin Hongguang Boiler Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongguang Boiler Company) to purchase 10 sets of 3MW low-temperature towers.

It was further ascertained that due to cracks, burns, and scratches on the foundation rings and flanges produced by Kaiming Company, the parties concerned held a site meeting in the tower workshop on April 26, 2011. On May 23, 2011, Kaiming Company notified Huarui Company of the potential risks associated with the steel plates and promised to propose a solution as soon as possible. Regarding the issues of cracks in the foundation rings and flange curling, the parties held several meetings thereafter to negotiate solutions, including third-party inspections, return to factory for repairs, adjustments to production and welding processes, and engaging experts through Huarui Company. Through the joint efforts of the parties, all 64 sets of foundation rings and 55 sets of tower bodies delivered by Kaiming Company have been installed and have passed inspection and acceptance by Huarui Company.

On July 5, 2010, Huarui Company and Kaiming (Daqing) New Energy Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kaiming New Energy Company) signed a "Strategic Cooperation Agreement," agreeing to leverage their respective strengths to cooperate in the construction of wind power projects, promoting mutual development and growth. The parties were to offer each other the most favorable prices and services to ensure the smooth implementation of the projects. On September 5, 2010, Huarui Company entered into a "49.5MW Wind Power Project Wind Turbine Generator Set Sales Contract" with Zhaoyuan Xinlong Shunde Wind Power Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinlong Shunde Company). On the same day, Huarui Company and Kaiming New Energy Company entered into a "Wind Turbine Generator Set Sales Agreement." On July 13, 2011, Kaiming New Energy Company notified Huarui Company that it was terminating the "Wind Turbine Generator Set Sales Agreement" and the "49.5MW Wind Power Project Wind Turbine Generator Set Sales Contract" between Huarui Company and Xinlong Shunde Company.

Huarui Company and Lvyuan Company entered into a "Equipment Late Delivery Compensation Agreement," which recorded that Lvyuan Company and Huarui Company had signed contracts for the supply of wind turbine equipment for the Daqing Heping, Aobao, Xinli, and Wukeshu wind farms. Due to Huarui Company's untimely supply, the hoisting work for the wind turbine equipment was severely delayed, resulting in total downtime losses for the four wind farms of RMB 9,537,233. Considering that Lvyuan Company's failure to make timely payments due to insufficient funds was also a cause of the untimely supply, the parties agreed through negotiation that Huarui Company would compensate for downtime losses in the amount of RMB 6.5 million, and Lvyuan Company would bear the remaining losses itself.

The People's Bank of China further specified the benchmark lending rates for financial institutions during the following periods: from October 20, 2010 to December 26, 2010, the benchmark rate for loans with a term of six months or less was 5.10% per annum; from December 26, 2010 to February 9, 2011, the rate for loans with a term of six months or less was 5.35% per annum; from February 9, 2011 to April 6, 2011, the rate for loans with a term of six months or less was 5.60% per annum; from April 6, 2011 to July 7, 2011, the rate for loans with a term of six months or less was 5.85% per annum and the rate for loans with a term of six months to one year was 6.31% per annum; from July 7, 2011 to June 8, 2012, the rate for loans with a term of six months or less was 6.10% per annum and the rate for loans with a term of six months to one year was 6.56% per annum; from June 8, 2012 to July 6, 2012, the rate for loans with a term of six months or less was 5.6% per annum and the rate for loans with a term of six months to one year was 6% per annum.

A dispute arose between the parties regarding the delivery of goods and payment of货款 under the contract in question.

Kaiming Company filed a lawsuit, requesting a judgment: (1) to order the continued performance of the contract, with Huarui Company accepting the remaining 9 sets of tower barrels; (2) to order Huarui Company to pay RMB 112,009,744 in tower barrel purchase price; (3) to order Huarui Company to pay interest for delayed payment until the date of actual payment; (4) to order Huarui Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Huarui Company filed a counterclaim, requesting a judgment: (1) to order Kaiming Company to pay compensation for delayed delivery in the amount of RMB 11,877,776; (2) to order Kaiming Company to pay RMB 6.5 million for losses from claims by the owner; (3) to reduce the unit price of tower barrels from RMB 12,140 per ton to RMB 9,950 per ton, reducing the total contract price by RMB 42,852,920; (4) to order Kaiming Company to issue a quality commitment letter conforming to requirements to Huarui Company regarding the quality of the goods; (5) to order Kaiming Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The Heilongjiang High People's Court held that the "Tower Barrel Sales Contract" entered into between Kaiming Company and Huarui Company on September 5, 2010 represented the true intention of both parties, its contents did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, there were no other statutory circumstances rendering the contract void, and it had been approved by the Heilongjiang Provincial Development and Reform Commission; therefore, the contract became effective on December 6, 2010. The court addressed the issues in this case as follows:

(1) Regarding the determination of the breaching party for the incomplete performance of the "Tower Barrel Sales Contract" involved in this case. After the contract was signed, on November 2, 2010, Huarui Company notified Kaiming Company of changes to the delivery time and quantity stipulated in the contract. Kaiming Company agreed to these changes, and both parties actually performed accordingly. Therefore, Huarui Company should have made advance payments and progress payments at each stage based on the total price of 64 sets of tower barrels. According to the contract, Huarui Company was to make payments in six installments based on the delivery schedule. Specifically, Huarui Company should have paid an advance payment of RMB 23,755,552 by January 8, 2011, but it only paid RMB 14 million. Huarui Company should have paid the first progress payment of RMB 47,511,104 by April 22, 2011, but it only paid RMB 20 million on April 26. Huarui Company should have paid the second progress payment of RMB 71,266,656 after the delivery of all foundation rings by October 19, 2011, but it failed to pay on time. By the time of Huarui Company's last payment on April 6, 2012 (which was after the due date for the fourth progress payment on January 3, 2012), Huarui Company had paid a total of RMB 124,388,880, which was still insufficient to cover the second progress payment. During the performance of the contract, Kaiming Company repeatedly demanded in writing the advance payment and progress payments from Huarui Company, but Huarui Company still failed to pay as agreed. Therefore, Huarui Company's overdue payment actions constituted a breach of contract. Although Huarui Company claimed that between July 2011 and April 2012, it had paid over RMB 25 million to Kaiming Company in four installments using bank acceptance drafts, which were rejected by Kaiming Company, it failed to provide sufficient evidence to support this claim. Moreover, the contract stipulated that payment by acceptance draft was conditional on payment within the agreed period. Huarui Company's use of forward acceptance drafts after defaulting on payment was not in accordance with the contract, and even if Kaiming Company rejected them, this did not violate the contract. Furthermore, even if these payments were included, Huarui Company still failed to fulfill its payment obligations as agreed. Although Kaiming Company did not deliver the goods at the times notified by Huarui Company during the performance of the contract, it had notified Huarui Company in writing that if payment was not made on time, the supply time would be delayed. Pursuant to Article 67 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), which provides: "Where the parties are mutually indebted and there is a sequence of performance, a party that is obligated to perform later has the right to reject the performance request of the party that should have performed first if the latter fails to perform. If the party that should perform first fails to perform its obligations as agreed, the party that is obligated to perform later has the right to reject the corresponding performance request." Huarui Company was obligated to first pay the advance payment and progress payments for each production stage. As previously explained, Huarui Company had been in breach from the very start regarding the advance payment. Therefore, Kaiming Company had the right to refuse Huarui Company's request for delivery of goods. Consequently, even if Kaiming Company did not deliver the goods on time, this did not constitute a breach of contract. As for Huarui Company's claim regarding product quality issues during the performance of the contract, although some product quality issues did exist in Kaiming Company's delivered goods during production, through the joint efforts of both parties, particularly the substantial assistance of Huarui Company, the quality issues that arose were promptly addressed. The 64 sets of foundation rings and 55 sets of tower barrels that were delivered had been installed and were all accepted as qualified by Huarui Company. Therefore, under the current circumstances, it cannot be determined that the products delivered by Kaiming Company still have quality problems. Huarui Company's defense and counterclaim that Kaiming Company's products had quality issues, leading to delayed delivery and constituting a breach of contract, lacked factual and legal basis. The court rejected the counterclaim seeking payment of late delivery penalties and compensation from Kaiming Company.

(2) Regarding whether Kaiming Company's claim for an increase in the tower barrel price could be established. According to the "Tower Barrel Sales Contract," "When the market price of plates and flanges fluctuates by more than or equal to 5% of the prices of plates and flanges in Appendix 1, the supply price shall be adjusted accordingly." However, the contract did not specify what constitutes "market price" or how the market price should be determined. During the trial, both Kaiming Company and Huarui Company acknowledged that there were numerous plate markets nationwide, and there was no unified market price. It was impossible to determine which region's price could represent the market price of plates. Additionally, the price of plates was influenced by factors such as region, brand awareness, product quality, dealer level, purchase quantity, transportation costs, and even negotiation skills. Both parties could not agree on a mutually recognized market price. Although Huarui Company argued that the market price of plates should be appraised, the parties could not agree on the basic conditions for determining the market price, such as which region, which level of dealer, and what quality standards should be used. Therefore, the conditions for judicial appraisal were not present in this case. Huarui Company also failed to provide evidence proving that the prices Kaiming Company paid to Aotong Company, Zhaojiayu Company, and Huahong Company for purchasing plates were significantly higher than those of other sellers under equivalent conditions. In fact, some of the quotation sheets from Aotong Company to Huarui Company showed that prices for certain plates under comparable conditions were even higher than Kaiming Company's actual purchase prices. Based on the existing evidence, it could be confirmed that the average ton price of plates actually purchased by Kaiming Company, RMB 6,300, was the market price. To determine whether this price met the adjustment conditions stipulated in the contract, it should be compared with the prices listed in Appendix 1 of the contract. Appendix 1 only stated that the weight of the tower barrel body and foundation ring was 261 tons, and according to the drawings, the average ton price of barrel body plates was RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% consumption). It did not specify the market price of plates at the time the contract was signed or the purchase price agreed upon by the parties. Both parties agreed that the comparison should be made on a uniform basis, either by comparing the average ton price of purchased plates or by comparing prices including consumption. However, the parties disputed the nature of the contractual term "average ton price of barrel body plates RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% consumption)." Huarui Company argued that this price included consumption and should be compared with the actual price of RMB 6,300/ton. However, the RMB 6,042.60/ton in the contract corresponded to the weight of plates in the finished tower barrel, which was 261 tons, not the total weight of plates required to produce one tower barrel. The contract's notation "including 6% consumption as RMB 6,042.6/ton" also indicated that this was not a purchase price. This price was not on the same basis as the actual average purchase price of RMB 6,300/ton and could not be directly compared. Given that Kaiming Company, in its letters to Huarui Company dated January 26, 2011, and February 15, 2011, had stated that the contract's average ton price of barrel body plates of RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% consumption) corresponded to an average plate purchase price of RMB 5,700.57/ton, and had listed the calculation method, and Huarui Company did not object to this in its reply but instead requested that Kaiming Company immediately order materials and that the contract price adjustment be discussed later, Huarui Company's position could not be sustained. The average ton price of plates purchased by Kaiming Company, RMB 6,300, increased by RMB 599.43 compared to the contractually stipulated RMB 5,700.57, representing an increase of 10.52%, which exceeded the 5% threshold agreed in the contract. Therefore, the supply price should be adjusted. As for how to adjust the supply price, although the parties indicated during the performance of the contract that they would discuss this issue, they failed to reach an agreement before and during the litigation. Since the fluctuation in plate prices was a normal market fluctuation, both parties had foreseen it at the time of signing the contract and had a clear solution. Therefore, this price increase constituted a normal market risk. Although the parties failed to agree on how to adjust the supply price, considering that the parties had expressly provided in the risk solution that if the price fluctuation did not exceed 5%, no adjustment was required — meaning that a price increase of no more than 5% was what Kaiming Company could and was willing to bear within its profit margin — any increase beyond that should not be borne by Kaiming Company. In light of this, Huarui Company should bear the portion exceeding 5%, i.e., the supply price increase of 5.52%, amounting to RMB 13,113,064.70.

(3) Regarding whether Huarui Company's claim for a reduction in the tower barrel price could be established. Huarui Company argued that Kaiming Company, Kaiming New Energy Company, and Xinlongde Company were affiliated companies, and the contracts it signed with the three companies were also related. Specifically, it argued that it purchased tower barrels from Kaiming Company only because Kaiming New Energy Company and Xinlongde Company purchased wind turbine generators from it, and that the tower barrel price was set at RMB 12,140/ton, which was far above the market price at that time. Now that Kaiming New Energy Company had terminated the wind turbine procurement contract with Huarui Company, the basis for the tower barrel price of RMB 12,140/ton agreed between Kaiming Company and Huarui Company had ceased to exist, and the price should be reduced to the then-market price of RMB 9,950/ton. Although the investors of Kaiming Company and Kaiming New Energy Company both included Hong Kong Kaiming Company, and Xinlongde Company was a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kaiming New Energy Company, the three companies were independent legal entities. The "Strategic Cooperation Agreement" signed between Huarui Company and Kaiming New Energy Company only provided that the parties would give each other the most favorable prices and services. None of the three contracts signed by Huarui Company stipulated that they were mutually dependent on each other or that the parties had therefore raised the contract prices. Therefore, Huarui Company's claim for a reduction in the contract price lacked factual and legal basis. If the termination of the contract by Kaiming New Energy Company caused losses to Huarui Company, it could assert its rights separately based on the principle of privity of contract.

(4) Regarding whether the 9 sets of tower barrels not accepted by Huarui Company should continue to be performed. As previously explained, Huarui Company was in breach of contract. Under these circumstances, without notifying Kaiming Company to stop production, Huarui Company purchased 10 sets of tower barrels from Hongguang Boiler Company on January 31, 2012. At the same time, on February 21, 2012, it sent a letter to Kaiming Company requiring strict delivery of one set every two days, and on March 19, 2012, it again sent a letter to Kaiming Company requiring that the final 9 sets of tower barrels be delivered in April 2012. However, after the 10 sets of tower barrels from Hongguang Boiler Company arrived on site on April 20, 2012, Huarui Company unilaterally terminated the contract, citing previous quality problems with Kaiming Company's tower barrels and concerns that Kaiming Company might not be able to deliver on time, and refused to accept the tower barrels produced by Kaiming Company. Its unilateral termination of the contract did not meet the conditions for termination under the contract or under the law, and its actions were contrary to the principle of good faith, constituting a breach of contract. Therefore, Kaiming Company's claim for continued performance of the contract was established, and Huarui Company should accept the remaining 9 sets of tower barrels.

(5) Regarding how to determine the amount of outstanding货款 owed by Huarui Company. Kaiming Company had already satisfied the conditions for delivery of the remaining 9 sets of tower barrels and had fulfilled its delivery obligation. Due to Huarui Company's unilateral refusal to accept them, the contract was not fully performed. Since the "Tower Barrel Sales Contract" stipulated that after all tower barrels were delivered to the site and accepted as qualified, Huarui Company would pay 15% of the total contract price, Huarui Company's refusal to accept the goods prevented the fulfillment of the payment condition. Therefore, at the time of Huarui Company's refusal to accept the tower barrels, the payment condition should be deemed to have been satisfied, and Huarui Company should pay for that portion of the goods in accordance with the contract. The contract stipulated that the final total price would be determined based on the tonnage verified by both parties according to the buyer's drawings. The parties had not verified the tonnage of the delivered tower barrels. Both parties now indicated that they could not verify the quantity mutually, and both had no objection to the contractually agreed price. Therefore, the total contract price should be the contractually agreed price of RMB 237,555,520 plus the plate price increase of RMB 13,113,064.7 to be borne by Huarui Company, totaling RMB 250,668,584.7. After deducting 10% warranty deposit of RMB 25,066,858.47 and the amount already paid by Huarui Company of RMB 124,388,880, Huarui Company still owed Kaiming Company RMB 101,212,846.23.

(6) Regarding whether Kaiming Company's claim for losses due to overdue payment could be established. Since the "Tower Barrel Sales Contract" did not stipulate liability for breach due to overdue payment, pursuant to Article 24, Paragraph 4 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Sales Contracts, which provides: "Where a sales contract does not stipulate liquidated damages for overdue payment or the method for calculating such damages, and the seller claims compensation for losses due to overdue payment on the grounds of the buyer's breach, the People's Court may calculate the compensation based on the benchmark interest rate for同类 loans of the People's Bank of China for the same period, with reference to the standard overdue penalty interest rate." Kaiming Company was entitled to claim compensation for losses from overdue payment. Considering the actual circumstances of this case, the losses for each period of default should be calculated based on the benchmark interest rate for同类 loans of the People's Bank of China for the same period plus a 40% increase. Specifically, Huarui Company owed RMB 9,755,552 in advance payment from January 8, 2011, until it was fully paid on March 1, 2011. The loss for this period was RMB 109,565. Huarui Company was required to pay the first progress payment of RMB 47,511,104 at the latest by April 22, 2011, when the foundation rings were delivered. It paid RMB 20 million on April 26, 2011, RMB 17.8 million on November 28, 2011, and RMB 9,711,104 on December 16, 2011. The loss for this period was RMB 1,596,608. Huarui Company was required to pay the second progress payment of RMB 71,266,656 at the latest by October 29, 2011, the 15th day after delivery of all foundation rings. It paid RMB 28,122,224 on December 16, 2011, RMB 20 million on December 31, 2011, and RMB 5 million on April 6, 2012. The second progress payment was still short by RMB 18,144,432. As of December 31, 2012, the loss on the second progress payment was RMB 2,765,363. Huarui Company was required to pay the third progress payment of RMB 35,633,328 by January 18, 2012, which remains unpaid. As of December 31, 2012, the loss on the third progress payment was RMB 2,944,699. Huarui Company was required to pay the fourth progress payment of RMB 35,633,328 by May 1, 2012, which remains unpaid. As of December 31, 2012, the loss on the fourth progress payment was RMB 2,053,217. Huarui Company should bear RMB 13,113,064.7 for the plate price adjustment. After deducting 10% warranty deposit, the remaining amount should have been paid by May 1, 2012. As of December 31, 2012, the loss on this amount was RMB 680,024. As of December 31, 2012, Kaiming Company's total loss was RMB 9,469,452. From January 1, 2013, to the actual date of payment within the automatic performance period specified in the judgment, the compensation shall be calculated based on RMB 101,212,846.23, using the benchmark interest rate for同类 loans of the People's Bank of China for the same period plus a 40% increase.

Furthermore, although Huarui Company also requested Kaiming Company to issue a quality commitment, the "Tower Barrel Sales Contract" had clear provisions on quality requirements and liability for quality breaches, and a 10% warranty deposit was reserved. Even if these provisions were incomplete, relevant laws provided for such matters. Huarui Company's request for Kaiming Company to issue an unconditional quality liability commitment letter lacked contractual and legal basis.

In summary, the Heilongjiang High People's Court, in accordance with Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 107, 109, 159, and 161 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 24, Paragraph 4 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Sales Contracts, ruled as follows: (1) The "Tower Barrel Sales Contract" shall continue to be performed, and Kaiming Company shall deliver the remaining 9 sets of tower barrels to Huarui Company within 30 days after the judgment takes effect; (2) Huarui Company shall pay Kaiming Company the outstanding tower barrel price of RMB 101,212,846.23 within 10 days after the judgment takes effect; (3) Huarui Company shall pay Kaiming Company compensation of RMB 9,469,452 for losses incurred up to December 31, 2012, and for the period from January 1, 2013, to the actual date of payment within the automatic performance period specified in the judgment, compensation shall be calculated based on RMB 101,212,846.23, using the benchmark interest rate for同类 loans of the People's Bank of China for the same period plus a 40% increase, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect; (4) Kaiming Company's other claims are rejected; (5) Huarui Company's counterclaim is rejected. The litigation costs for the main action, RMB 649,195.98, shall be borne by Kaiming Company in the amount of RMB 58,013.72 and by Huarui Company in the amount of RMB 591,182.26. The litigation costs for the counterclaim, RMB 347,958.48, shall be borne by Huarui Company. The preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Huarui Company.

Huarui Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court, arguing that: the first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law, and requested that the first-instance judgment be reversed and amended to: (1) dismiss all claims of Kaiming Company in the first instance; (2) order Kaiming Company to pay delayed delivery compensation of RMB 11,877,776; (3) order Kaiming Company to pay RMB 6,500,000 for the owner's claim losses caused by its delayed delivery; (4) order that the contract price per ton under the disputed Tower Barrel Sales Contract be reduced from RMB 12,140 to RMB 9,950, and the total contract price be reduced from RMB 237,555,520 to RMB 194,701,600; (5) order Kaiming Company to issue a quality commitment letter conforming to requirements to Huarui Company regarding the quality of the delivered goods; (6) Kaiming Company shall bear the litigation costs of the first instance and second instance. The facts and reasons supporting its appeal are:

(I) Regarding the determination of the breaching party. During the performance of the contract, Kaiming Company committed acts of breach. 1. Kaiming Company's refusal to accept the banker's acceptance bill constituted a breach, but the first-instance judgment failed to accept the objective fact that Huarui Company had previously paid Kaiming Company by banker's acceptance bill which was refused, constituting unclear finding of fact. 2. According to the contract, Huarui Company was only obligated to pay 30% of the purchase price in advance. In fact, after the advance payment was fully made, Kaiming Company still delayed delivery, causing delays in the tower barrel installation works; its conduct constituted a breach. The first-instance judgment found that although Kaiming Company did not deliver the goods according to the time notified by Huarui Company, it had notified Huarui Company in writing that if payment was not made on time, the delivery time would be delayed, and thus even if Kaiming Company did not deliver the goods on time, it did not constitute a breach.

(II) Regarding whether Kaiming Company's claim to increase the tower barrel price can be established. The contract price for steel plates was RMB 6,042.6 per ton. The market prices of plates and flanges were compared with this price to determine whether to adjust. There is no evidence to prove that RMB 6,042.6 per ton corresponds to the actual weight of 261 tons of tower barrels excluding consumption. In fact, RMB 6,042.6 is a price that includes 6% consumption and has not yet been excluded. If the contract's stipulation "average ton price of barrel plates RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% consumption)" is considered to correspond to these 261 tons, then the contract should have stipulated "excluding 6% consumption" rather than "including 6% consumption". The first-instance court, based on an erroneous determination of the nature of the average price of RMB 6,042.6 per ton, concluded that the price had increased by more than 5% and adjusted the contract price accordingly, which is erroneous.

(III) Regarding whether Huarui Company's claim to reduce the tower barrel price can be established. The determination of the contract prices in the Tower Barrel Sales Contract and the Wind Turbine Generator Sales Contract in this case is interrelated. Kaiming New Energy Company's unilateral rescission of the Wind Turbine Generator Sales Contract completely destroyed the basis for determining the price in the Tower Barrel Sales Contract. If performance continues according to the original contract, it would result in manifest unfairness, and the principle of change of circumstances should be applied to modify the contract. Huarui Company's counterclaim for reduction of the contract price should be upheld.

(IV) Regarding whether the nine sets of tower barrels not accepted by Huarui Company should continue to be performed and whether the corresponding payment should be made. Because Kaiming Company lacked the corresponding technical capability and production experience, it had various serious quality defects in the production and delivery of the foundation rings and tower barrels under this contract, directly causing Kaiming Company's inability to complete delivery within the mutually agreed delivery period, thereby causing serious delays in the installation and construction plan of the wind farm owner and resulting in huge economic losses. The mutually confirmed delivery period was March 15, 2011 (64 sets of foundation rings) and June 15, 2011 (64 sets of tower barrels). In actual contract performance, Kaiming Company only delivered the first set of foundation rings on April 22, 2011, and the first set of tower barrels on August 17, 2011. Because Kaiming Company repeatedly broke promises and could not deliver on time, to ensure the construction progress of the wind farm owner, and for the sake of preparedness, Huarui Company purchased 10 sets of tower barrels from Hongguang Boiler Company on January 31, 2012. The first-instance court's determination that Huarui Company "unilaterally terminated the contract on the grounds of previous quality problems with the tower barrels and concerns that Kaiming Company could not deliver on time" did not meet the conditions for rescission and constituted a breach, which is erroneous. The extensive evidence submitted by Huarui Company in the first instance can prove that Kaiming Company had serious breaches of delayed delivery, which were continuous and caused serious consequences; Huarui Company repeatedly urged and gave Kaiming Company multiple opportunities to remedy, and only terminated the contract when it could no longer tolerate the situation. This act has sufficient legal basis.

(V) Regarding whether Kaiming Company's claim for losses due to overdue payment can be established. Huarui Company paid Kaiming Company by bank acceptance bill but was unreasonably refused. The refusal had no contractual basis, and the relevant payment should not bear interest; the nine sets of tower barrels were not actually delivered and were not inspected according to Article 8.2 of this contract, so the conditions for payment were not met and interest should not be calculated; the so-called "increased tower barrel price" payment cannot be established at all, and certainly should not bear interest; Kaiming Company's failure to receive payment on time according to this contract is directly related to its own breaches of serious quality defects and delayed delivery, and it should bear corresponding liability for breach. The first-instance court should not have calculated the penalty interest at 40% above the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period.

Kaiming Company argued in defense that: (I) It did not breach the contract. The reasons are: 1. Kaiming Company did not refuse the banker's acceptance bill. Although it explicitly stated its refusal to accept the banker's acceptance bill, it did not actually refuse to accept it, but instead continued to receive three batches of acceptance bills totaling RMB 14 million. Therefore, Huarui Company's claim that Kaiming Company refused the banker's acceptance bill lacks sufficient evidence, and any allegation of breach based on this has no basis. 2. Kaiming Company did not delay delivery. The contract stipulated that delays should be recognized by both parties through contract modifications. Although the parties did not formally modify the contract to re-stipulate the delivery period, during performance, the delivery period was changed multiple times through correspondence, and the actual conduct also confirmed the modification of the contract, which should be deemed a modification of the contract. From the start of performance, Kaiming Company began urging Huarui Company in writing to pay the advance payment. Huarui Company's failure to pay the full amount on time should bear the responsibility for delayed delivery. (II) The price of the subject tower barrels should be increased. According to Appendix 1 of the contract, per the drawings, the average ton price of barrel plates is RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% consumption). This RMB 6,042.6 is the converted purchase price, not the direct purchase price. The contract stipulates the direct purchase price as RMB 5,700 (RMB 6,042.6 / 1.06), which is the price excluding consumption. Kaiming Company's actual purchase price for plates was RMB 6,300, which is also the price excluding consumption. Comparing the two results in a price increase of 10.52%, which is correct. Article 4 of the contract stipulates: when the market price of plates and flanges fluctuates by more than or equal to 5% of the price of plates and flanges in Appendix 1, the delivery price shall be adjusted accordingly. Therefore, the delivery price should be adjusted. (III) Huarui Company's claim for a reduction of the tower barrel price has no basis. 1. Whether the contract price in this case should be increased or decreased should be based on the contract. As stated above, Article 4 of this contract has clear provisions on price adjustment. The adjustment here is not limited to increases but also includes decreases. If the market price of plates decreases by more than 5% after the contract is signed, the overall contract price should also be reduced accordingly, and Kaiming Company must also bear this consequence. The price adjustment is binding on both parties, and the rights and obligations are reciprocal. 2. The contract in this case is not related to the price of the contract outside this case. Because the contract does not explicitly stipulate a price correlation; the two contracts outside this case were signed by different civil subjects, and according to the principle of privity of contract, a subject that does not enjoy rights or assume obligations under a contract cannot become a bearer of liability. 3. The circumstances claimed by Huarui Company for the application of the principle of change of circumstances simply do not exist, and the principle of change of circumstances is not applicable in this case. 4. Huarui Company's refusal to accept the nine sets of tower barrels was malicious and should bear the obligation of continued performance and payment of the corresponding price. 5. According to the relevant provisions of the Judicial Interpretation of the Contract Law, Huarui Company should compensate for losses due to overdue payment.

In summary, all of Huarui Company's appeal claims and reasons are untenable and should be dismissed according to law.

During the second instance, Kaiming Company submitted "Applications for Continuation of Property Preservation" to this Court on November 5, 2013, and February 10, 2014, respectively. Upon review, the grounds for its applications were established, and this Court accordingly notified the Heilongjiang High People's Court to handle the continuation procedures.

The facts of this case as found by this Court are substantially consistent with those found in the first instance.

After the conclusion of the second-instance trial, this Court presided over mediation between the parties, but ultimately no mediation agreement was reached.

This Court holds that: the first-instance judgment's determination that the subject Tower Barrel Sales Contract is valid is correct, and this Court affirms it. Based on the parties' allegations and defenses, this Court summarizes the disputed issues between the parties in this case as follows: (I) whether the floating price of the subject goods should be adjusted; (II) whether Kaiming Company committed a breach and should bear liability for breach; (III) whether the nine sets of tower barrels not accepted by Huarui Company should continue to be performed; (IV) whether Kaiming Company's claim for losses due to overdue payment is established; (V) whether Huarui Company's first-instance claims should be upheld. Each issue is discussed in turn below.

(I) Regarding whether the floating price of the subject goods should be adjusted.

This Court holds that: Kaiming Company actually purchased 17,350 tons of tower barrel plates, paying a total of RMB 109,304,462.58, with an average price per ton of RMB 6,299.97. According to Article 4.1 of the Tower Barrel Sales Contract, when the market price of plates and flanges fluctuates by more than or equal to 5% of the price of plates and flanges in Appendix 1, the supply price shall be adjusted accordingly. Appendix 1 of the contract stipulates: "Average ton price of barrel plates RMB 6,042.6 (including 6% consumption)." The portion of the actual purchase price of barrel plates exceeding the contract price by more than 5% shall be borne by Huarui Company. However, the actual floating rate during performance was 4.26%, i.e., the ratio of the contract's average price per ton of RMB 6,042.6 to the actual average purchase price per ton of RMB 6,299.97. Accordingly, the contract price should not be adjusted. Kaiming Company's calculation, using the price of RMB 5,700.566 after deducting 6% as the base ratio against the actual average purchase price of RMB 6,299.969, resulting in a supply price increase of 10.52%, shifts the 6% consumption that Kaiming Company should bear onto Huarui Company, which is inconsistent with the contract. Huarui Company's claim that the supply price increase was less than 5% has factual basis, and this Court accepts it. The first-instance judgment's determination that the supply price increase was 10.52% is erroneous and should be corrected. The first-instance judgment's confirmation of Huarui Company's liability for the additional plate price increase of RMB 13,113,064.7 should be deducted from the payable amount. Specifically: the total contract price of RMB 237,555,520, deducting 10% quality guarantee deposit of RMB 23,755,552 and the RMB 124,388,880 already paid by Huarui Company, Huarui Company should still pay Kaiming Company RMB 89,411,088. Given that nine sets of tower barrels with a contract value of RMB 33,406,245 have not yet been delivered, 60% of the advance payment and progress payment for the goods, amounting to RMB 20,043,747, should be deducted according to the contract. The remaining RMB 13,362,498 should be deducted from the total payable amount of RMB 89,411,088. After deduction, Huarui Company should pay Kaiming Company the overdue payment of RMB 76,048,590 plus interest, and the remaining RMB 13,362,498 shall be paid within 15 days after delivery of the nine sets of tower barrels.

(II) Regarding whether Kaiming Company committed a breach and should bear liability for breach.

This Court holds that: 1. Regarding whether Kaiming Company refused the bank draft. According to the contract, Huarui Company had the right to choose to pay by bank draft. Although Kaiming Company stated in some receipts that refusing the bank draft did not comply with the contract, it actually accepted the bank drafts, which does not constitute a breach. As for Huarui Company's claim that the bank draft was returned because Kaiming Company refused it, due to insufficient evidence, this Court does not accept it. 2. Regarding whether Kaiming Company delayed delivery. Given that the parties changed the contractual delivery time through correspondence during performance, the changed delivery time should be used to determine whether there was a delay. Accordingly, it should be determined that Kaiming Company had delayed delivery. 3. Regarding quality defects in the delivered goods. Although quality issues were found in the tower barrels delivered by Kaiming Company, Kaiming Company promptly carried out repairs, the project passed acceptance, and no engineering quality issues were found during the warranty period. Therefore, the goods should be deemed to have passed quality inspection, and Kaiming Company should not bear liability for compensation.

(III) Regarding whether the nine sets of tower barrels not accepted by Huarui Company should continue to be performed.

This Court holds that: Kaiming Company delivered these nine sets of tower barrels within the delivery period and did not breach the contract. If the tower barrels that it invested heavily to produce according to the contract cannot be sold, it will suffer huge economic losses. The conditions for Huarui Company to exercise its right to terminate the contract had not been fulfilled, and its unilateral termination does not have the effect of termination. Huarui Company's actions violated the principles of sanctity of contract and contractual fairness. Its claim that the nine undelivered sets of tower barrels should no longer be delivered is unsupported and this Court does not uphold it. The first-instance judgment's order that Huarui Company continue to perform the contract is not improper and should be affirmed.

(IV) Regarding whether Kaiming Company's claim for losses due to overdue payment is established.

This Court holds that: interest is the fruits generated from principal. Huarui Company's long-term non-payment of a substantial amount of the purchase price to Kaiming Company constitutes a breach, thereby causing Kaiming Company interest losses. Although Huarui Company claims that Kaiming Company unreasonably refused the bank draft, there is insufficient evidence, and it cannot be exempted from liability for paying interest on the purchase price. Therefore, its claim that the relevant payment should not bear interest is not supported by this Court. In this case, Kaiming Company did not request Huarui Company to pay interest at 40% above the benchmark loan interest rate. The first-instance judgment's order for Huarui Company to pay interest at 40% above the benchmark loan interest rate exceeded Kaiming Company's first-instance claims. Therefore, this Court does not uphold the part of the interest at 40% above the benchmark loan interest rate, but upholds the interest on the overdue payment. Accordingly, the judgment is amended to calculate the interest on the overdue payment at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period and same type.

(V) Regarding whether Huarui Company's first-instance claims should be upheld.

Huarui Company's first-instance claims involve four issues: 1. Whether Kaiming Company should pay delayed delivery compensation of RMB 11,877,776. This Court holds that: although Kaiming Company delayed delivery, because Huarui Company was in arrears with progress payments from the beginning of contract performance, and after delivery was long overdue, despite multiple written demands from Kaiming Company, Huarui Company still deliberately delayed payment, causing difficulties for Kaiming Company to purchase tower barrel materials. This conduct had a direct impact on the delayed delivery. Moreover, when Kaiming Company demanded payment, it had already informed Huarui Company in writing that if payment was not made in time, delivery would be delayed, which is consistent with Article 15.3 of the Tower Barrel Sales Contract. Accordingly, the parties modified the delivery time, and even up to the delivery of the last nine sets of tower barrels, Huarui Company, before the delivery period had expired, purchased and used tower barrels from a third party. Therefore, Huarui Company's claim that Kaiming Company should pay it RMB 11,877,776 in delay compensation is not supported by this Court. 2. Whether Kaiming Company should pay the owner's claim losses of RMB 6,500,000. This Court holds that: First, the delay compensation under Article 16 of the Tower Barrel Sales Contract does not include compensation for losses to the owner, and Huarui Company's claim has no contractual basis. Second, although Huarui Company agreed with the owner to pay RMB 6,500,000 for delay losses, it has not yet paid the owner, and the losses should not be deemed to have occurred. Therefore, Huarui Company's claim lacks basis and is not supported by this Court. 3. Whether the tower barrel price should be reduced from RMB 12,140 per ton to RMB 9,950 per ton. This Court holds that: both Kaiming Company and Kaiming New Energy Company are independent legal persons. According to the principle of privity of contract, Kaiming New Energy Company's unilateral rescission of the Wind Turbine Generator Sales Contract belongs to another legal relationship. If there is any dispute, it should be handled according to the contract and legal provisions. In this case, the performance of the Tower Barrel Sales Contract by both parties did not involve a situation of serious imbalance of interests, so the principle of change of circumstances cannot be applied. Huarui Company's claim does not comply with the relevant provisions of the Judicial Interpretation of the Contract Law, and therefore its request to reduce the tower barrel price is not upheld. 4. Whether Kaiming Company should issue a quality commitment letter to Huarui Company. This Court holds that: the quality guarantee deposit is in the nature of a guarantee. Clause 5.4.1 of the Tower Barrel Sales Contract stipulates, "If the buyer's losses are caused by manufacturing quality issues, the relevant amounts shall be deducted from the quality guarantee deposit." The parties have already withheld 10% as a quality guarantee deposit from the purchase price according to the contract, the purpose being to compensate for any quality issues that may arise with the tower barrels. Therefore, Huarui Company's request for Kaiming Company to additionally issue a quality commitment letter has no contractual basis. The first-instance judgment's denial of Huarui Company's request in this regard is correct.

In summary, the findings of fact in the first-instance judgment are substantially clear, but the application of law was erroneous and should be corrected. Part of Huarui Company's appeal reasons have factual and legal basis and should be upheld. In accordance with Article 170(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

(1) Affirm Items 1, 4 and 5 of the civil judgment (2012) Hei Gao Shang Chu Zi No. 9 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court;

(2) Reverse Item 3 of the civil judgment (2012) Hei Gao Shang Chu Zi No. 9 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court;

(3) Amend Item 2 of the civil judgment (2012) Hei Gao Shang Chu Zi No. 9 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court to read as follows: Huarui Windpower Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. shall pay the outstanding tower barrel purchase price totaling RMB 89,411,088 to Daqing Kaiming Wind Power Tower Manufacturing Co., Ltd., of which RMB 76,048,590 shall be paid within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, and the remaining balance of the purchase price for the nine sets of tower barrels, RMB 13,362,498, shall be paid within 15 days after delivery;

(4) Huarui Windpower Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. shall pay to Daqing Kaiming Wind Power Tower Manufacturing Co., Ltd. interest on the overdue payment of RMB 76,048,590, calculated from the date the payment fell due in accordance with the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period and same type, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The case acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 649,195.98, of which RMB 129,839.20 shall be borne by Kaiming Company and RMB 519,356.78 by Huarui Company; the case acceptance fee for the counterclaim is RMB 347,958.48, which shall be borne by Huarui Company.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 939,140.74, of which RMB 118,236.45 shall be borne by Kaiming Company and RMB 820,904.29 by Huarui Company.

This judgment is final.
